answer: Stake-weighted entry, one bond per verified operator. Keys are free, so a Sybil ring mints many addresses, but weight counts per bonded operator, not per address; splitting funds across keys equals one key. Reaching 30% of rewards forces the attacker to lock 30% of the bonded pool plus a bond and proof cost per extra seat, and no seat inherits proof from neighbors. The ledger is a beacon: correlated funding clusters, so a knoll of fresh mirror addresses is flagged and its rewards freeze until each proves separate history, so each identity is a deposit. Cost rises with N; payout is flat.
